excerpt: Selling ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, and digital downloads with automated crypto delivery — no platform middleman, no payout delays, no geographic filter.

content.text: Selling a digital product should be a simple transaction. You build something valuable — an ebook, a course, a Notion template, a font family, a preset pack, a beat — and someone pays you for access to it. The file transfers. The transaction completes. But for millions of creators, the payment layer is where everything breaks down. Stripe is unavailable. PayPal flags the account. Gumroad holds the payout. The workarounds stop working. What actually works is a sovereign commerce stack: a static storefront on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, automatic payment verification through NOWPayments, and delivery triggered by a webhook the moment the transaction confirms on-chain. No platform intermediary. No payout schedule. No geography filter. The customer owns the storefront code, the order history, the customer list, and the product files. COREMERCH has no access after deployment.
What This Actually Is and Why It Matters

The automated delivery pipeline for digital products follows a specific sequence that eliminates every manual step. A buyer visits the storefront, selects a product, and initiates payment. The checkout displays a QR code with the exact wallet address and payment amount in their chosen cryptocurrency, converted from USD at the current exchange rate via live price feeds. The buyer sends the payment from their wallet. NOWPayments monitors the blockchain and detects the incoming transaction within seconds of broadcast. When the transaction receives sufficient confirmations on-chain, NOWPayments fires a webhook to your Cloudflare Worker or Google Apps Script endpoint. The backend verifies the payment amount, confirms the transaction hash on the blockchain directly, logs the order, generates a receipt, and sends the download link to the buyer's email address. Total time from payment confirmation to delivery email: under 30 seconds in almost all cases.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

Pricing digital products in crypto is straightforward because NOWPayments handles the currency conversion automatically. You set your price in USD. The checkout pulls live exchange rates and displays the exact amount in whichever cryptocurrency the buyer selects — Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT, Solana, or any of 300+ supported coins. The buyer always pays the USD equivalent at the time of transaction. For USDT-denominated products, there is no conversion at all — one dollar in equals one dollar received, minus network fees that typically amount to less than $0.10 on Tron or Solana. You receive the crypto equivalent of your USD price in the wallet you configured in your NOWPayments account. COREMERCH never touches these funds at any point — the wallet is yours from the moment of setup.
Who This Is Built For and Why

The product types that work with automated crypto delivery are any digital files that can be stored and delivered via download link: ebooks in PDF or EPUB format, courses packaged as ZIP archives or delivered via hosted video links, Notion templates exported as files or share links, font families as ZIP archives of OTF and TTF files, Lightroom or Capture One preset packs, beat files as WAV or MP3 archives, plugin installers, stock photo packs, software license keys, and any other file-based product. The delivery system in Stack 01 uses Google Drive shared links. Stack 02 uses Cloudflare R2 presigned URLs with configurable expiry times — typically 24 to 72 hours — which prevents download links from being shared indefinitely after a single purchase. Both approaches work reliably and cost nothing beyond the storage used.
Automated delivery means the download link arrives before the buyer navigates away from the payment confirmation page.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The order management layer gives you complete visibility into every transaction your store processes. In Stack 01, every order is logged to a Google Sheet with the buyer's email, product purchased, payment amount in crypto and USD equivalent, transaction hash for on-chain verification, and delivery status. In Stack 02, orders are stored in a Supabase PostgreSQL database with the same fields plus additional metadata. Both can be exported as CSV at any time. The transaction hash provides cryptographic proof of every payment that does not depend on any platform's records — you can verify any transaction independently on a public blockchain explorer. This level of transparency and verifiability is structurally different from conventional payment processors, where transaction data is owned by the platform and subject to their record-keeping policies.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

Scaling a sovereign digital store requires no infrastructure changes at any realistic volume level for most individual creators. Cloudflare Workers processes each webhook event independently — ten simultaneous orders are handled as ten separate processes with no queue congestion. Supabase handles hundreds of concurrent database operations on the free tier. Resend delivers 3,000 emails per month on the free tier — enough for significant daily sales volume. Cloudflare Pages serves the storefront to any number of concurrent visitors without capacity constraints. NOWPayments processes payment volume without per-transaction approval delays. The Sovereign Blueprint documents exactly when and how to upgrade each layer of the stack as volume increases — which thresholds trigger which upgrades, and how to migrate without any downtime. The infrastructure that works on day one is the same architecture that works at ten times the volume.
